about: What a GENERATED Kotlin artifact answers differently from ECMA-262 for a
reason that is not about the language at all.
`kotlin_lua_divergences.json` beside this file is about the two ROUTES
into the Lua engine — what the frontend lowers at build time, and what
the engine lowers at run time — and both of its arrays are empty. This
file is about the CODE GENERATOR, and it exists because
`ecma262-lowered-kotlin` found something on the day it was built that
neither of those routes could be blamed for.
Keeping the two apart is the whole point. Folding a code-generation
defect into a language-divergence list would make
`kotlin_lua_divergences.json` non-empty and would say the frontend gets a
case wrong, which is false and would send the next reader to the wrong
half of the seam.
HELD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by `LoweredEcma262ArtifactTest`. An entry whose
case the artifact now answers CORRECTLY is red — remove it, because a
list that can only grow can never reach zero, and zero is the point. An
undeclared wrong answer is red too. Neither direction has an escape
hatch: a case is either right, or named here with a cause someone can
act on.
AND A CEILING. `MAX_DEFECTS` in that suite refuses a list that has grown
past a handful, and `ecma262-lowered-kotlin` keeps a SECOND ceiling over
the `codegen-defects=` count the suite prints — in another language, so
raising the constant in the file that reads it is not enough. An
exclusion list with no ceiling is a way to make any lane green, and this
one is small on purpose: every entry is a defect someone is expected to
remove, not a property of the backend.
⚠ THE LIST IS EMPTY, AND IT GOT THERE THE WAY IT WAS MEANT TO. It held
exactly one entry, from 2026-08-30: the generated Kotlin evaluated a
transition's `cond` TWICE — once to choose the target and again in
`executeTransitionActions` to choose which arm's content to run — so
`++v == 2` incremented, took its transition, incremented again, and
recorded the other arm's answer. The repair is the one the entry's own
`fix` named: `TransitionResult` now carries a machine-wide
`transitionIndex`, the dispatch switches on it, and no guard is
evaluated twice. The suite then went RED — 'declared … and the artifact
answers it correctly. The defect is fixed: remove the entry' — on both
routes, which is what made removing it a measurement rather than a
decision. That red is the direction this list exists for; without it the
list could only grow.
An empty list is therefore the intended steady state, not a sign the
file is unused. It is the contract that KEEPS it empty: an undeclared
wrong answer is red, and so is a declared one that has stopped being
wrong.
